summary: Home looks finished, but several of its controls write to the economy without evidence or undo. The hero's Daily goal ticks pay XP and gold on every re-tick. Streak milestone bonuses are paid again every day because the milestone key is derived from a streak that can end 'yesterday'. Reminder and habit ticks have no Undo. Reports still hard-code the three exam subjects: a week led by Code or Japanese is saved with the words 'undefined took the largest share', and study-space time is missing from every subject split. Reports also save empty weeks for a brand-new account (hasContent counts the shipped plan) and freeze 'quiet' weeks saved before history arrives. As a personal OS, Home still answers 'what next' only for CS/Maths/IT, the calendar and reminders: Code, Japanese, Mind, Creatives and Money have no rung. The Continue row hides Mind and Creatives off-screen. Smaller layout issues: touch targets under 44px on text-link buttons, dead space in equal-height cards, the iPhone XP row with almost no slack, and an exam rung that lasts past the exam.
coverage: Continued from an interrupted earlier auditor (15 findings kept, not repeated). This run (slot 2): a DOM measurement scan (overflow, ellipsis clipping, text overlap, touch targets, ovals) of #/home, #/reports, a week page, its study/focus/collection overviews and a month page at mac 1470x832, ipad 820x1180 (coarse pointer) and iphone 402x874, on the seeded and the empty (reset) account. Screenshots looked at: Home iPhone (XP row), Home mac full with a routines fixture, the empty Home and Reports on mac, a Reports index full page at iPhone, the Focus overview at iPhone, Home in Dawn at iPhone, a week report in the Celestial Duality shop theme on mac, and the Kurenai-words failure. Behaviour fixtures: reminder tick and toast; milestone re-pay (today's study removed, then a todo logged); directive tick/untick x4; Code and Japanese Focus sessions against Home's split and the report template; Focus card 90m Start; focusPlan at 09:00/15:00/23:30; background-redraw scroll keep; reset and backfill; Read the report and New state. Matrix in findings/home-reports.inventory.md. NOT checked by this run: Up next rungs other than the exam rung (study block lead, deadline at risk, start-by, assignment estimate, next exam within 6 weeks; budget); term and year pages (no term saved in this seed; the earlier auditor's r-term/r-year shots exist); story player and share/export (covered by the earlier auditor); the iPhone XP overlap in real Safari (no WebKit in the harness, so Chromium geometry only); Goals switch persistence; the iPad landscape scan (ipadl) for Reports. Harness note: the app sets data-theme on <body>, so the harness's --theme flag alone does not re-theme; screenshots used --js to set body.dataset.theme.

findings.title: Mind and Creatives are pushed off-screen in Home's Continue row (fixed subject order, 4 visible, no scroll affordance)
findings.detail: Continue renders one desk per started subject in the fixed KOS.subjects order (compsci, maths, it, code, ja, mind, creatives) and then Collection, in a grid with grid-auto-columns = a quarter of the width and overflow-x:auto. With Code and Japanese started (the user's case), Mind is the 6th and Creatives the 7th column: at 1470x832 they sit at x=1766 and x=2072 inside a 1210px-wide row (scrollWidth 2434) and Collection at 2378. macOS hides the thin scrollbar, there are no arrows, no fade, no count, so the desks never appear. A second, smaller cause: KOS.mind.started()/KOS.creatives.started() only become true once a lesson page has recorded a read (state.mind.lessons / state.creatives.lessons|works); a Daily 15, Journal entries or Positions alone never put Mind on Home. Reproduced: fresh seeded account, opened Mind F1.1, Creatives A1.1, Code 1.1, Japanese H1 -> desks order compsci:236, maths:542, it:848, code:1154, ja:1460, mind:1766, creatives:2072, coll:2378.
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-mac-continue.png; eval of .k-desks: clientWidth 1210, scrollWidth 2434; js/modules/hub.js:1558-1563 (filter + fixed SUBJECTS order); css/views/home.css:183 (grid-auto-columns quarter width, overflow-x:auto); js/core/mind.js:430, js/core/creatives.js:255 (started())
findings.fix: Order the study desks by recency (last studied time from the ledger / ui.lastRef timestamps) so what you are doing is always in the first four; make the row wrap into a second line on desktop/iPad (auto-fill minmax columns) or add visible prev/next buttons and an edge fade with a 'N more' count; let started() also count Mind's Journal/positions/cards and Creatives' works.
findings.devices: mac, ipad landscape (4 across), ipad portrait (2 across)
findings.rootCause: Fixed registry order plus a 4-column horizontal scroller with no affordance; started() reads only lesson records.

findings.title: Weekly/monthly reports saved before the history arrives are frozen as 'A quiet week for study' forever
findings.detail: ensureReports() runs at boot and saves every backfilled week since 1 September. The skip rule for an empty rebuilt week is hasContent(), which counts f.plan and f.tasks; the shipped Pacing seed gives every fresh install plan facts, and the LATEST week is saved whatever it holds. So the first boot on an empty device (a new iPad/iPhone before sign-in finishes its first pull, or before a backup is restored with importFull, which does not touch kurenai-os-reports) saves weeks with mins:0 and the month 'October 2026 · a quiet month for study'. Reports are never recomputed (getReport hit -> skip), so after the history arrives Home's Reports card still says 'A quiet week for study · 0m studied' while Study hours on the same screen shows 9.2 h and the ledger has focus sessions on 20, 21, 22, 23 and 25 Oct. Reproduced: reset -> first boot -> seed: week:2026-10-19 and week:2026-10-12 both have facts.study.mins 0, createdAt = the reset boot, while weeks saved during the seed have real minutes.
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-mac-all-desks.png (Week in review card 0m beside Study hours 9.2); eval KOS.reportStore.cached(): week:2026-10-19 {mins:0,sessions:0} created 1793576817945; ledger has type focus on 2026-10-20..25; js/core/reportstore.js:228-231 (hasContent counts plan/tasks), :275-279 (latest week always saved, a saved report is never rebuilt)
findings.fix: Do not let plan/tasks alone make a rebuilt week 'content'; hold the first ensureReports until the first cloud pull has completed (or until KOS.cloud says signed-out), and after importFull / first cloud link re-run the backfill with a 'replace rebuilt reports whose facts are empty or older than the newest ledger entry in their period' rule (rebuilt reports were never shown as final anyway).
findings.rootCause: Save-once reports are created from an incomplete ledger; hasContent treats seeded Pacing rows as activity.

findings.title: iPad portrait Home has no Daily goal, no Today's three, no Recovery list and no Start focus in the hero
findings.detail: css/views/home.css hides .k-home-goal entirely in the 1080px tier and only shows it again under 700px. Between 701 and 1080 (the iPad Air 11" in portrait, 820x1180, and Split View) the hero loses its whole right column: the directive list, the Morning Review's Today's three (roadmap 5.10, frame 33t) with its ▶ Start, and in Critical HP the Recovery checklist and 'Open Recovery →' (invariant 2's recovery route). Measured: .k-home-goal display:none, rect 0x0 at 820 wide; the hero shows only ring, greeting and level line.
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-ipad.png (hero without Daily goal); eval at --size ipad: goal display none; css/views/home.css:221-223 (@media (max-width:1080px){.k-home-goal{display:none}}), :244 (re-shown only under 700)

findings.devices: ipad portrait, iPad Split View, any 701-1080 window

findings.title: Home does not answer 'what next' for Code, Japanese, Mind, Creatives or Money
findings.detail: Home's render reads KOS.srs.dueCards (flashcards only), calendar, assignments, reminders, pacing, goals, routines and the media stats, but never KOS.code.planDay (the Daily 20), KOS.ja.due/planDay, KOS.mind.planDay (the Daily 15), KOS.creatives.planDay (the Daily Creative) or KOS.money notices (bill in two days, trial ending, budget). KOS.today.build, which invariant 149 makes the one source for the reviews and Home's three, does not read them either. So with Code started, the Daily 20 is 'Your first program' and Home says nothing; Japanese facets, Code retrieval cards and Mind cards due are not in 'Review N due cards'; a bill due tomorrow appears only in the bell. Money appears nowhere on Home (innerText has no money/bill/budget). The study-space desks in Continue are the only trace, and they are scrolled off-screen (see the Continue finding).
findings.evidence: eval: KOS.code.planDay() -> lesson 1.1 'Your first program'; KOS.mind.planDay() and KOS.creatives.planDay() return day plans; Home innerText matches no money/bill/budget; js/modules/hub.js:1041-1730 (reads list); js/core/today.js (no ja/code/mind/creatives/money reads)
findings.fix: Give KOS.today.build a 'spaces' read (each space's planDay summary: Code Daily 20, Japanese reviews + next lesson, Mind Daily 15, Creatives Daily Creative) and a money read (KOS.money.notices(today,{hide}) and safe-to-spend), then: count all due cards in the Due card (split by space), add the spaces' daily items as Up next rungs / Today rows, and a compact Money line (next bill, left this month) on Home.
findings.rootCause: Home and the day model predate the study spaces and Money; each space built its own daily plan without registering it with the day model.

findings.title: Home 'Study hours' and Reports 'Studied' measure different things (12h14m vs 2h32m for the same week)
findings.detail: Home's Study hours card (hoursOn / hoursThisWeek / sessionsThisWeek) sums dur of EVERY non-media ledger entry - notes, reading, quiz, exam, tracker, flashcards, and todo ticks (invariant 4: activity, never study) - while KOS.report's study() counts only type 'focus' minutes as 'Studied' (its days count uses isStudy, so 'Studied 2h 32m · 5 sessions · 7 days'). For week 28 Sep-4 Oct the ledger gives 734 min by Home's rule and 152 min by the report's. Home's card links 'Weekly reports ›' straight under its figure, so the two numbers contradict each other one click apart; the Study overview's '5 sessions · 7 days' is self-contradictory too. Invariant 26d says study statistics are derived once.
findings.evidence: eval over state.sessions 2026-09-28..10-04: non-media dur 734 min, focus dur 152 min; js/modules/hub.js:917-921 (hoursOn), :636-649; js/core/report.js:185-200, :254; /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-report-0928-study.png
findings.fix: Define study minutes once (e.g. KOS.sessions.studyMins(range), using isStudy + parts) and have Home, Reports, Goals' study-hours type and the Daily goal all call it; exclude todo/external and media; if non-Focus activities count, count them in Reports too (or say 'Focus time' on both).
findings.rootCause: Two independent minute definitions (hub.js vs report.js).

findings.title: Streak milestone bonuses are paid again every day: before the first study session the streak 'ends yesterday', which moves each milestone's key date by one day
findings.detail: governor.js keys each milestone to the date the run reached it, computed as today - (stk - ms). KOS.sessions.streak() counts the run ending TODAY if there is study today, otherwise ending YESTERDAY. So on any morning, the first non-study session (a reminder or habit tick on Home, a routine, a todo) sees stk one lower with today's date, works out a key date one day later than the stored one, and pays 3+7+14+30 (+60/+100) gold again with four '35-day streak' notes. Once the first study session of the day logs, the run ends today again, the key dates move back, and they pay once more. Reproduced on the seeded account: today's 6 study entries removed, then one todo session logged; gold went 12531 -> 12586 (+55 = 1 for the tick + 54 in milestones); milestones moved from streak30:'2026-10-31' to '2026-11-01'; toast '+5 XP · +55 gold · 35-day streak, 35-day streak, 35-day streak, 35-day streak'. Ticking a reminder on Home with study already done today also paid +55 the first time (see study-core's milestone-note finding for the retro-pay and the note text). This is a daily gold leak of up to 2 x 54 (2 x 214 past 100 days), against invariant 1.
findings.evidence: eval reproduction (slot 2, seeded): gold [12531,12586,12587], m0 vs m1 above; js/core/governor.js:330-339; js/core/sessions.js:166-175 (streak ends today or yesterday); Home tick: js/modules/hub.js:1199 (KOS.reminders.complete then rerender), toast '+5 XP · +55 gold · 36-day streak x4'
findings.fix: Key a milestone to the run's start date (the first day of the run, which does not move whether it ends today or yesterday), e.g. runStart = lastActiveDay - (stk-1), and store the run start once per milestone. Better: pay a milestone only on the session that makes the streak reach exactly ms days ending today. Note ms, not stk, in the text.
findings.rootCause: The milestone key is derived from today's date and a streak length that refers to a run which may end yesterday

findings.title: Report words print 'undefined took the largest share' when Code, Japanese, Mind or Creatives got the most Focus time, and that text is saved for good
findings.detail: report.js study() adds every stretch's subject to bySubject, including code, ja, mind and creatives. reportwords.js largestShare() picks the biggest key, but SUBJECT only maps compsci/maths/it, so the template writes SUBJECT['code'] = undefined. Reproduced: a 5h Code Focus session and 1h Japanese this week, then KOS.report.build(this week) + KOS.reportWords.template -> narrative 'undefined took the largest share, 6h of 8h 06m, across 6 sessions on 5 of 7 days.' A week's words are written once when it is saved (invariant 102), so the broken sentence stays on the Reports page, the Home card, the share card and the notification. The same keys feed the month/term/year narrative at reportwords.js:93 ('…: undefined 6h, Maths 49m').
findings.evidence: eval (slot 2, seeded + qa Code/ja focus sessions): bySubject {maths:49, it:17, code:360, ja:60}, narrative 'undefined took the largest share…'; js/core/reportwords.js:17 (SUBJECT has 3 keys), :45-50, :93, :138-141; js/core/report.js:30 (SUBJECTS = compsci, maths, it), :196-199 (inc(bySubject, pt.subject) for any subject)
findings.fix: Name subjects through KOS.subjects.name(sid) (and their hue through KOS.subjects) everywhere in report.js, reportwords.js, reports.js, reportstory.js, reportshare.js; add a smoke case with a Code-heavy week. Consider re-generating template words for saved reports whose narrative contains 'undefined'.
findings.rootCause: Reports hard-code the three exam subjects although the ledger carries seven

findings.title: Hero 'Daily goal' directives pay XP and gold on a self-tick with no evidence, and untick/re-tick pays again without limit
findings.detail: Each directive in the hero (e.g. 'Clear 308 due flashcards (245 overdue)') is a button that calls KOS.todo.setChecked(key, !on). Ticking logs a 'todo' session (+5 XP, +1 gold, counts as the day's activity for HP). Unticking only deletes the check and refunds nothing. Ticking again logs another session and pays again. Reproduced: four taps in a row gave XP 71807 -> 71812 -> 71812 -> 71817, gold 12531 -> 12532 -> 12532 -> 12533, sessions 601 -> 603. The 308 cards were still due. So the hero rewards claiming the goal rather than doing it (KurenaiOS's rule elsewhere is status from evidence), and the economy can be farmed by tapping. The first tick of a day also triggers the streak milestone re-pay (see the milestone finding). The ✓ is the only feedback; the count goes '1 / 5'.
findings.evidence: eval (slot 2 seeded): [[71807,12531,601],[..,'false'],[71812,12532,602,'true'],[71812,12532,602,'false'],[71817,12533,603,'true']]; js/modules/hub.js:1162-1169; js/modules/todo.js:56-69 (log on tick, no reversal on untick)
findings.fix: Derive the directive's tick from its evidence (cards due cleared, the exam's revision minutes met, the assignment's progress), as KOS.todo's auto items should. If a manual tick stays, pay once per key per day (store the paid key) and never on re-tick, or pay nothing (activity only, like external ticks, invariant 160).
findings.rootCause: Legacy generated to-do list's manual tick logs a paid session each time it becomes true

findings.title: Hero 'Daily goal' counts 5 items but shows only 3, with no way to reach the other 2
findings.detail: The goal head prints autos.filter(checked).length + ' / ' + autos.length (0 / 5) but only autos.slice(0,3) are drawn and there is no '+2 more' link; the two hidden directives cannot be seen or sealed from Home. 'Start focus →' under the list is generic (opens Focus blank) while Today's three variant starts the first item; the hand-tick lets 'Clear 308 due flashcards' be sealed without doing anything.
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-mac-all-desks.png (DAILY GOAL 0 / 5, three rows); js/modules/hub.js:1153-1173
findings.fix: Show '+N more' linking to the full list (Routines Today / Reminders), or count only what is shown; make Start focus start the first unchecked directive like Today's three does; let auto items tick themselves from evidence rather than by hand.
findings.rootCause: slice(0,3) for display but the full length in the counter.

findings.title: Hero's season chip ('Autumn · by season') covers the Daily goal count
findings.detail: The art chip is absolutely positioned top-right of the hero (inset 14px/16px, z-index 2) and is always visible on touch devices (hover:none) and on hover with a mouse. It lands on the goal head: at 1180x820 chip [980..1140, 94..126] over the head [878..1128, 104..122], hiding '0 / 5'; on the Mac the same overlap appears whenever the pointer is over the hero (chip [1270..1430] vs head [1168..1418]). On the iPhone the chip sits 3px above the date kicker.
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-ipadl-hero-crop.png; css/components.css:703-705; js/modules/hub.js hero goal head
findings.fix: Reserve space for the chip in the hero (padding-block-start on .k-home-goal when the hero has art) or move the chip to the bottom-right/after the goal list; on touch, make it a small icon button.

findings.title: Report Focus heat map drops every block between 23:00 and 07:00 (late-night study vanishes; contradicts the Night Owl line)
findings.detail: KOS.report builds the heat grid only for hours 07-22 (HEAT_FROM 7, HEAT_TO 23) and silently discards minutes outside it, while the persona counts 21:00-04:00 as 'late'. Week of 28 Sep: Focus card says '5 blocks · 2h 32m', facts.focus.hours has 55 min at 02:00 and 40 at 06:00, but the heat grid holds only two cells (33 and 24 min) - three of five blocks are invisible, under a 'Night Owl · 36% of your Focus came after 21:00' line that has nothing lit after 21:00. The user studies past midnight (Home greets 'Working late' at 00:05).
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-report-week-0928.png; eval facts.focus.heat vs hours/list; js/core/report.js:33, :321, :336, :369
findings.fix: Make the grid span the hours that actually hold focus (min/max of the period's hours, at least 07-23), or fold the night into a labelled 23-07 column; word the persona with the range it measured ('after 21:00 or before 04:00').
findings.rootCause: Fixed 07-23 grid window with no overflow bucket.

findings.title: Share/Export dialog stays open across navigation (Back, swipe-back, hash change) and shows the previous report over another page
findings.detail: Open Share on Reports › Week of 28 Sep, then go Back or change the hash (#/reports, #/home): the router re-renders #main under the modal but never closes it. The share sheet for 28 Sep stays over the 19-25 Oct report and even over Home, scroll-locked. On the iPhone/iPad Home Screen app the OS back gesture triggers exactly this. Reproduced by eval: dialog open count 2 before, 2 after location.hash='#/reports', 2 after history.back().
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/reports-iphone.png (28 Sep share sheet over the 19-25 Oct report); /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/home-dawn-mac.png (same sheet over Home); js/core/router.js:284-306 (onPop renders without closing dialogs); js/core/ui.js:155 openDialog
findings.fix: In router renderRoute/onPop, close every open KOS.ui dialog (call its close, which restores focus) before rendering; or have openDialog push a history entry so Back closes the dialog first (the iOS sheet convention).
findings.rootCause: openDialog and router are not coordinated; navigation does not dismiss modals.

findings.title: Home's middle rows leave large empty areas inside equal-height cards (Today, Due today, Study hours, Week in review)
findings.detail: The 3-column rows stretch every card to the tallest one. Measured at 1470x832 (seeded): Today with 'Nothing on today' ends ~200px above its card bottom (card 306px tall); Due today's last row ends at y=661 and its Start reviewing button sits at y=729 (68px of nothing); Study hours on a Monday morning or an empty week draws a ~140px empty plot under the goal line; the Week in review card for a quiet week draws an empty 7-bar chart plus '0m studied' (~120px). The empty account shows the same (Today and Study hours). This breaks the standing 'no dead space' rule.
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-mac-all-desks.png, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/home-dawn-mac.png, /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/empty-home-mac.png; eval: .k-upnext 326px tall, last row bottom 661, button top 729
findings.fix: Let Today's empty state collapse and give the freed height to Upcoming/Goals (align-items:start plus masonry like Reports' pack), or fill it with the next timed item tomorrow / the next lesson day; pin Due today's button directly under its rows; hide the hours plot (keep figures) when the week has no minutes and the report chart when facts.study.chartDays is false.

findings.title: Upcoming caps at 3 rows: two overdue assignments hide the mock exam 4 days away, with no 'N more' and a link to Assignments only
findings.detail: The Upcoming card draws up to two overdue assignments and then counts.slice(0, 3 - urgent) countdowns. Seeded: NEA (4 days overdue), Assignment 3 (2 overdue), Assignment 8 (in 3 days) - while 'AQA 7517 Paper 2 ... mock - 4d away' is in the hero's daily goal but absent from Upcoming. There is no '+N more' line, and the only way out is 'Tracker →', which opens Assignments (not the Exams hub or the Calendar's countdowns, where exams, start-by dates and plan milestones live). The '4'/'2'/'3' discs carry the day counts with no unit beside them (the sub-line repeats it).
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-mac-all-desks.png (Upcoming), hero daily goal lists the mock; js/modules/hub.js:1430-1458

findings.title: iPhone hero: the XP line shares a row with the 200px XP bar and has 6px of slack, so it collides as soon as glyph metrics or the number grow
findings.detail: At 402px the level line is a wrapping flex row: 'Level 53 · Grandmaster', then the bar (flex 0 1 200px) and '2398 XP to 54' side by side on the second line, then HP. In Chromium the text sits 10px after the bar's end and ends at x=340 in a 310px content box (36..346), so only 6px is left. In the screenshot the dark track runs right up to the mono text, so the bar and the number read as one shape, which is the overlap the user sees. Chromium does not show the glyphs overlapping (bar 36-236, text 246-340; with '12398 XP to 154' the text ends at 354, past the box). Safari on the phone was not available to the harness. Either way the layout depends on a fixed 200px bar width plus the width of a mono string.
findings.evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/home-reports/b4-home-iphone.png, /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-home-iphone-hero.png; eval --size iphone: .k-bar rect x36 w200, '.k-home-level .k-mono' x246..340, box 36..366 minus padding; css/views/home.css:31-34 (.k-home-level flex-wrap, .k-bar flex 0 1 var(--home-xp-w)); css/tokens.css:393 (--home-xp-w: 200px); js/modules/hub.js (level line markup: b, span.k-bar, span.k-mono, dot, hp)
findings.fix: Under 700px make the bar its own full-width row (flex-basis 100%) with the 'N XP to L' text right-aligned on the row above it beside the level name, or use a grid: [level name | XP to next] over [bar spanning both]. Drop the fixed 200px basis.
findings.rootCause: Fixed-width bar plus nowrap mono text sharing one flex line with almost no slack

findings.title: Touch targets under 44px on Home's week plan and across Reports (tick boxes 18x18, '31 more this week' 19px, crumbs 20px, 'Full overview ›' 19px, 'What is sent' 19px)
findings.detail: With a coarse pointer (iPad 820 and iPhone 402) the DOM scan finds: Home's week plan tick checkboxes 18x18 (5 rows), '31 more this week' 104x19; Reports' breadcrumbs 'Reports' 48x20 and 'Week of 19 Oct' 92x20, 'ⓘ What is sent' 88x19, each card's 'Full overview: …' link 85x19, '+ 7 more carried over' 118x18, and the Study overview's topic links 300x20. Invariant 69 asks for 44px on a coarse pointer. Buttons get the base.css height rule, but these are k-link, k-rp-crumb, k-rp-more and k-rp-textbtn text buttons and a bare checkbox, which it misses.
findings.evidence: measure script (scratchpad measure.js) at --size ipad and iphone: Home small=['Tick off … <input> 18x18' x5, '31 more this week <button.k-plan-more> 104x19']; #/reports/week/2026-10-19 small=['Reports <button.k-rp-crumb> 48x20','ⓘ What is sent 88x19','Full overview: Study 85x19', …]; #/reports/week/…/study '4.5.4.1… <button.k-rp-tlink> 300x20'
findings.fix: Under (pointer: coarse), give k-link/k-rp-crumb/k-rp-more/k-rp-textbtn/k-rp-tlink a min-block-size of var(--hit-coarse) with inline padding (or a ::before hit area that does not overlap neighbours), and wrap the plan checkbox in a 44px label hit area.
findings.rootCause: The coarse-pointer minimum is applied to .k-btn and native buttons with padding, not to the text-link button classes

findings.title: Home's one-tap reminder and habit ticks complete and pay at once with no Undo
findings.detail: A tap on a Reminders row on Home calls KOS.reminders.complete(id, true) and redraws: the row disappears, XP and gold are paid and the toast has no Undo button. A mis-tap on a phone (rows are 44px with nothing between them) loses the reminder from the list and Home offers no way back; you have to go to Reminders, find it under completed and untick it, which does not take back the pay. The habit rows in the Routines card do the same through KOS.rtUI.tickStep. Elsewhere the app gives Undo for owner writes (invariant 144's pattern, the Money tools).
findings.evidence: eval: clicked [data-ui~=home.reminder-tick] 'Complete Email the exams officer…': toast '+5 XP · +55 gold · …', no button in #toast, the next row became first; js/modules/hub.js:1196-1200; habits: hub.js:1011-1014
findings.fix: Show the toast with Undo (KOS.ui.toast with an action) that calls KOS.reminders.complete(id,false) and reverses the session (or delay the pay for the toast's lifetime); the same for habit ticks.
findings.rootCause: Digest card added a write without the undo affordance used on owner pages

findings.title: A brand-new, empty account saves three weekly reports and a monthly one ('A quiet week for study', 0m) and Home announces them as '2 new'
findings.detail: After a reset (account created today, no sessions), ensureReports backfills and saves week:2026-10-12, -19, -26 and month:2026-10, all rebuilt, with study.mins 0 and days 0. Home's Week in review card shows '2 new' with 'A quiet week for study.' over an empty chart and 'October 2026 · A quiet month for study.'; Reports lists three identical quiet weeks with flat sparklines. Invariant 102 says an empty report is not saved. The guard hasContent() treats f.plan (the shipped Pacing seed, present for every week from the first day) and f.tasks as content, and the latest week is always saved. Weeks from before the account existed (state.created) are backfilled too.
findings.evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/home-reports/b4-empty-reports-mac.png, /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/home-reports/b4-empty-home-mac.png; eval after reset: week:2026-10-26/-19/-12 rebuilt=true {m:0,d:0}, month:2026-10 {m:0,d:0}; js/core/reportstore.js:228-231 (hasContent includes f.plan || f.tasks), :277-278 (latest week saved even when empty)
findings.fix: Do not backfill a period that ends before state.created (or before the first ledger entry); count the plan only when a row was ticked or carried in that period; skip the latest week when it has no study, focus, collection or tick content (keep the empty-state copy for Reports instead).
findings.rootCause: hasContent counts the seeded plan, which exists for every week, as content

findings.title: Study-space time is in the totals but missing from every subject split (Home's Study hours bar, Reports' Activity chart, legend, story)
findings.detail: Home's Study hours split is { compsci, maths, it } (hub.js:1500), and Reports draw bars and legends from SUBJECTS = compsci/maths/it (reports.js:37, 363, 710, 789, 1216, 1577; reportstory.js:84, 123). Logging 1h of Code and 1h of Japanese Focus today raised Home's total from 7.4 to 9.4 hours and 16 to 18 sessions, but the split stayed 'CS 1h · Maths 2.8h · IT 3.6h'. On Reports the day columns are drawn from the three subjects only, so a Code-only day draws as an empty or teal fallback column while the total counts it. The split no longer adds up to the number printed beside it (invariant 26d: a bar describes the value printed beside it).
findings.evidence: eval: Home before {big:'7.4 hours · 16 sessions', split:'CS1h Maths2.8h IT3.6h'}, after two 1h focus entries (code, ja) {big:'9.4 hours · 18 sessions +1.2h', split unchanged}; js/modules/hub.js:1500-1504; js/modules/reports.js:37, :1577-1579
findings.fix: Build the split from KOS.subjects.ids() (or the keys present) with each subject's hue; group the study spaces as 'Spaces' if the bar gets too busy.
findings.rootCause: Pre-5.3 three-subject lists kept in Home and Reports

findings.title: Home's Focus card and hero keep saying 'Revise for <exam> · at 14:00' after the exam has been sat (all evening)
findings.detail: Rung 2 of KOS.homeFocusPlan takes every exam from KOS.calendar.deadlines() inside its lead time and never checks the time of an exam that is today. With the seeded IT exam 'Revision block 28' at 14:00, focusPlan(today 09:00), (15:00) and (23:30) all return 'exam | Exam today | Revise for Revision block 28 | IT · at 14:00', and 'Start focus' starts a 25-90 min session 'for' an exam that has finished. Home's Today card already drops a timed event once it is over (kos-polish-3), so the two cards disagree. The hero's directive 'Revise for: Revision block 28 — today' has the same problem.
findings.evidence: eval: KOS.homeFocusPlan(new Date(today+'T15:00')) and ('T23:30') -> 'exam | Exam today | Revise for Revision block 28 | IT · at 14:00'; js/modules/hub.js:787-815 (exam rung, no time test); the session it starts: state.focus.active {mode:'custom', workMin:90, subject:'it', refs:[], objective:'Revise for Revision block 28'}
findings.fix: In rung 2, skip an exam dated today whose time (or end time) has passed, and fall through to the next rung (a post-mortem/log result prompt would be the natural next step: 'Log how Revision block 28 went'). Apply the same filter to the hero directive generator.
findings.rootCause: Lead-time test is by date only

findings.title: Weekly report page: the Study and 'Governor and Kurenai' cards are stretched to the Focus card's height and are mostly empty
findings.detail: On a week's page at 1470 (seeded week of 5 Oct, Celestial Duality theme) the three cards in the second row share one height (308px). Study holds a split bar and one top topic, leaving 168px empty. Governor and Kurenai holds two rows (Study streak, Rest streak), leaving 201px empty. Invariant 102a and the standing layout rule ('no page leaves dead space … uneven cards deal into measured masonry columns') are not met for this row. The 'Topics 1' stat tile has no caption either, where its neighbours have one.
findings.evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/home-reports/b4-report-celestial-mac.png; eval --size mac on #/reports/week/2026-10-05: Study h308 empty 168, Governor and Kurenai h308 empty 201; month 2026-09 Study h348 empty 98
findings.fix: Let the row use the masonry/pack path (align-items:start plus measured columns), or move Governor and Kurenai under Study in one column beside Focus; give the Topics tile a caption (e.g. 'touched' or the top topic).

findings.title: Home Goals list: the ring's number (days left) has no unit and is hidden from assistive tech
findings.detail: In Upcoming ▸ Goals each goal shows a ring with a bare number (39) — it is days until the period ends, while the ring's fill is percent done. Nothing says 'days', and the ring is aria-hidden so screen-reader users lose the days-left figure entirely; 'Too early to call' chips are low contrast on the card.

findings.fix: Print '39d' (or 'days' under the figure) and include it in the row's accessible text (e.g. '39 days left').

findings.title: Focus overview headline and persona contradict ('most of them before noon' beside 'Night Owl'), and blocks outside 07-23 are drawn at the 07 edge
findings.detail: reportwords.js picks ', most of them before noon' when share(4,12) >= 0.5 while report.js picks Night Owl first when share(21..4) >= 0.35; week 28 Sep satisfies both (64% 04-12, 36% 21-04), so the page says '5 Focus blocks, most of them before noon.' next to 'Night Owl - 36% of your Focus came after 21:00'. The 'Every Focus block' ribbon clamps a 02:28 Sunday block and a 06:20 Friday block to the 07 gridline ('Longest session Fri 06:20' in Study is drawn at 07:00).
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-fj-Developer-KurenaiOS---Web/083a292e-9158-4ad4-8d86-0c9b8abd3917/scratchpad/qa/shots/home-reports/seed-report-0928-focus.png; js/core/reportwords.js:192; js/core/report.js:366-371
findings.fix: Derive the headline clause from the persona (or order the tests the same way) and widen the ribbon axis to the period's real first/last hour.
findings.rootCause: Two independent time-of-day classifiers with different windows.

findings.title: Week's plan card header wraps 'Pacing →' onto its own line and truncates every row title
findings.detail: In the 415px column the header holds title, '23 behind', '0 of 13 · w/c 2 Nov' and an 84px segment meter, so the Pacing link drops to a second line at the left (1055,858) unlike every other card whose link is right-aligned on the title row. findings.title: Week report text says 'across 6 sessions on 7 of 7 days' next to a chart that shows Thursday at zero
findings.detail: The template narrative mixes two measures: 'sessions' counts Focus sessions only (report.js study(): sessions++ only for type focus), while 'days' counts any study entry (flashcards, quiz, exam). For the seeded week of 26 Oct the page says 'IT took the largest share, 1h 16m of 2h 23m, across 6 sessions on 7 of 7 days', but the Activity chart (Focus minutes) shows nothing on Thursday. Read together, '6 sessions on 7 days' looks wrong.
findings.evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS - Web/audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/shots/home-reports/b4-reports-iphone-full.png; js/core/report.js:183-188 (studyDays from any isStudy entry, sessions from focus only), :254; js/core/reportwords.js:140

findings.title: Routines card hides most habits with no 'N more' (a due routine leaves room for 2; an odd count drops one)
findings.detail: homeRoutines shows at most 4 habits, only 2 while a routine is due, and an odd count is rounded down to keep the grid even, so 3 habits show 2 and 5 show 4. While a routine is due the header shows 'Morning Routine due now' in place of 'N of M habits today', so with 5 habits Home shows 'Drink water' and 'Stretch' and gives no sign that 3 more are due today. findings.title: Exam revision time on Home is matched by the session's objective text, so renaming the exam (or two exams with one title) breaks the goal
findings.detail: 'Goal: N min of 2h for this exam today' counts a session as revision for an exam when metrics.objective === 'Revise for ' + ev.title, or when its topics meet the exam's topics. A session started from the card carries no exam or assessment id (state.focus.active has objective text only, refs [] for an exam with no topic links). If you rename the exam after studying, today's minutes drop to 0; two exams called 'Mock' share each other's minutes.
findings.evidence: js/modules/hub.js:790-800 (examMins by label); eval of state.focus.active after Home's Start focus: objective 'Revise for Revision block 28', no examId/eventId
findings.fix: Carry the event/assessment id on the session (metrics.examId) when it starts from the Focus card and count by id; keep the label match only for old entries.
findings.rootCause: Identity by display text

findings.title: Home jumps up 43px on a redraw when you are at the bottom: the Collection desk's rows are filled after the render
findings.detail: The Collection desk is drawn empty and filled by an async full-table mediadb.stats read (invariant 8). During KOS.rerender({background:true}) the page is briefly 1408px tall instead of 1451, so a scroll position at the bottom (679) is clamped to 636 and stays there once the rows arrive. Mid-page positions are kept. On the phone, where Continue is the last section, a background redraw (cloud pull, habit auto-tick) moves the view.
findings.evidence: eval --size mac: scrollTop 679 -> 636 after KOS.rerender({background:true}); at 400 the position is kept (scrollHeight 1408 right after the render, 1451 after 800ms); js/modules/hub.js:1601-1606 (empty medRows/medFoot), :1645 fillCollectionCard
findings.fix: Reserve the desk's rows (min-block-size, or render the last known stats from a per-device cache and update in place) so the page height does not change during the redraw.
findings.rootCause: Async fill after a synchronous redraw with no reserved height

findings.title: Reports count a title as active in the period for ANY journal event — a score change, a status tidy-up or a sync echo — so titles with no real progress appear in a week's Collection (and its story, genres, flows)
findings.detail: js/core/report.js collection() (about :446-456) touches a row for every journal event inside [start, end): (r.journal||[]).forEach(ev => if (ev[0] >= a && ev[0] < b) touch(r)). The media journal (mediadb.js, invariant 99) records progress, volumes, status, score, route, chapter and hours. So changing a score, or moving an old title to Completed or On hold as a tidy-up, counts as having watched or read it this week. The DI-27 echo (volumes null→N on every sync) made Death Note and Aku no Kyouten appear every week too. The touched set feeds the week's titles, byModule counts, genre and studio/author tallies, the genre-flow, and the stories. The user reported it 8 Nov: 'titles who haven't had actual progress made in the time frame should not appear, e.g. changing a score should not count as something having been done this week.' The 'Recently updated' vault sort is a separate reader (updatedAt); a score edit is a real edit there, but a no-op pull must never restamp it (invariant 36a; DI-27 broke this for the two rows).
findings.evidence: js/core/report.js:452-456 (every journal kind); js/core/mediadb.js journalFacts/journalDiff (score is a journalled kind); user report 8 Nov in chat.
findings.rootCause: 'Activity' is not defined. Reports treat the journal as a list of things done, but it is a list of fields changed.
findings.fix: Define activity once (one derivation, invariant 26d): progress, volumes, chapter, route or hours moving FORWARD, a start or finish date in the period, or a media session that names the row. Score, notes, tags and status moves without progress (onHold, dropped, planned, a 'completed' with no progress in range) are list edits and do not make a title active. Keep them for a separate 'list changes' line if wanted. Apply it in collection() and anything else that reads the journal for activity (Home and Collection 'this week', goals). Add a smoke: a score-only week shows no title.
